Apple varieties and rootstocks in India

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Old Indian orchards rely on Royal and Red Delicious. New high-density blocks plant high-colour strains (Scarlet Spur-II, Red Chief, Super Chief, Oregon Spur, Jeromine, Red Velox) and Gala, always with 25–33% compatible diploid pollinizers such as Golden Delicious, Granny Smith, Redlum Gala, Fuji or Manchurian crabapple. Warm valleys use low-chill HRMN-99, Anna or Dorsett Golden (Himachal package of practices, SKUAST-J, NIF).

Pollinizers: the most common cause of poor fruit set

Delicious apples cannot set fruit with their own pollen. Plant 25–33% diploid pollinizers (30–50% in cold or rainy valleys) that flower at the same time: Golden Delicious, Granny Smith, Redlum Gala, Fuji, or flowering crabapples such as Manchurian or Snowdrift. Avoid triploids such as Mutsu and Jonagold, whose pollen is sterile. Place 4–6 beehives per hectare (2–3 per acre) at 10–15% bloom, clear flowering mustard weeds that pull bees away, and never spray at full bloom (SKUAST-J, HortiKashmir).

Questions farmers ask

Which apple variety is best in India?

It depends on altitude: Royal Delicious and spur strains at 5,500–7,500 ft, high-colour strains such as Jeromine and Red Velox at lower belts, Gala for early markets, and low-chill HRMN-99 or Anna in warm valleys.

Which variety is the best pollinizer for Royal Delicious?

Golden Delicious is the classic choice; Granny Smith, Redlum Gala, Fuji and Manchurian crabapple also work. Plant 25–33% of trees as pollinizers.

Which apple can grow in warm areas?

Low-chill HRMN-99, Anna and Dorsett Golden need only 250–500 chilling hours. HRMN-99 is self-fertile; Anna and Dorsett Golden need each other.

Which rootstock is best for apple?

M.9 for deep, fertile, irrigated land with trellis; MM.106 for well-drained non-clay soil; MM.111 for drier, shallow hill soil; seedling for steep, unirrigated slopes.
